title: williamjblair/lean-proofs
summary: Machine-checked Lean 4 proofs of solved research problems from the Erdős problems collection, hosted as stable formal_proof targets for Google DeepMind's Formal Conjectures. The principal result is an affirmative answer to Erdős Problem #730 (Erdős, Graham, Ruzsa and Straus, 1975): the set of pairs n < m for which binom(2n, n) and binom(2m, m) have the same set of prime divisors is infinite, and in fact contains infinitely many consecutive pairs (n, n + 1). The proof formalises the argument posted informally by Liam Price on the problem's discussion page on 24 June 2026: Kummer's theorem…

formalizes.title: Comment on Erdős Problem #730 asserting, with a one-paragraph gist, that GPT Pro proves infinitely many consecutive pairs (n, n+1)

Closing derivation ('Proof Route Mapping') linked as a follow-up, reproducing the algebraic skeleton of the argument; the analytic sections exist only in a private document and are reconstructed in this formalisation
